belief: If my body is cremated, God can’t raise it.
meta: A Christian look at the fear that if your body is cremated God can’t raise it, with Scripture, questions, and homework for resting in the truth.
origins: Worry about a loved one who was cremated. Teaching that cremation is forbidden or makes resurrection impossible. Thinking of resurrection as God needing all the original pieces. Fear of what will happen to your own body. Christians hold different views about whether burial or cremation is better, but the question here is whether God is able.
teaches: Whatever happens to a body, God is able to raise it. Bodies return to dust in the grave, are lost at sea, or are destroyed in fires, and God promises that the sea and the grave will give up their dead. The God who formed you in secret and created the heavens and earth by His power says nothing is too difficult for Him. The resurrection does not depend on how a body is laid to rest but on the power of God.
self_statements: My loved one can’t be raised because of cremation.

errors: Picturing God’s power as limited by physical conditions.
Fearing the worst about a loved one’s future.
Blaming yourself for a choice that does not limit God.
Assuming resurrection must reassemble exact pieces.
questions: What happens to every buried body over time?
Are people lost at sea or in fires beyond God’s reach?
What does Jeremiah 32:17 say is too difficult for God?
Who created my body in the first place?
Does resurrection depend on human preservation or on God’s power?
Is my fear coming from Scripture or from something I heard?
Can I trust God with my loved one’s body?
truth: Cremation does not keep God from raising a body. Every body returns to dust, and God promises to raise the dead from the ground, the sea, and every place. Nothing is too difficult for Him. The resurrection depends on God’s power, not on how a body is laid to rest. I can trust Him with my body and my loved ones.
